foundation.description: Low-level contracts, deterministic tooling, and infrastructure intended to support many repositories.
expectations: Treat compatibility changes as deliberate contract changes.
Require deterministic validation before relying on the repository broadly.
Require real consumer evidence before promotion to reusable or stable maturity.

shared-platform.description: Reusable domain or platform capabilities consumed by multiple products, tools, or templates.
expectations: Keep ownership boundaries explicit and avoid product-specific behavior in shared APIs.
Validate representative consumers for material contract changes.
Prefer one canonical implementation over parallel local copies.

product.description: Vertical user-facing application, service, or specialized tool that composes shared foundations.
expectations: Optimize for complete user-facing behavior rather than horizontal extraction.
Reuse shared foundations where they are proven instead of creating local alternatives.
Keep end-to-end acceptance evidence close to the product behavior.

lab.description: Experimental proving ground used to learn before promoting a capability into a durable owner.
expectations: Allow rapid change without promising compatibility.
Keep experiments isolated from stable consumers until promotion is explicit.
Record the intended promotion or retirement decision when evidence is sufficient.

template.description: Canonical starter or reference repository whose contract is the generated consumer experience.
expectations: Validate generated or representative consumers rather than only the template repository itself.
Keep toolchain and migration intent explicit.
Prefer shared packages and reusable workflows over copied implementation logic.

experiment.description: A spike or early implementation whose contract may change freely.
experiment.promotionEvidence: A concrete use case and a clear owner are required before promotion.

proving.description: A real use case exists and the repository is gathering evidence about the right boundary.
proving.promotionEvidence: Promote only after repeated use demonstrates that the boundary is durable.

reusable.description: The repository has demonstrated reuse and is expected to serve multiple real consumers.
reusable.promotionEvidence: At least two genuine consumers or equivalent independently verified reuse should exist.

stable.description: The repository exposes a deliberately supported contract with strong deterministic and consumer evidence.
stable.promotionEvidence: Compatibility discipline, authoritative validation, and representative consumer checks are required.

maintenance.description: Feature growth is intentionally limited while compatibility, security, consolidation, or retirement is managed.
maintenance.promotionEvidence: A repository leaves maintenance only through an explicit renewed product or platform decision.
